facts.statement: The type species Parahesperornis alexi was originally described as Hesperornis gracilis and later reassigned to the genus Hargeria before being moved to Parahesperornis.
facts.quote: Parahesperornis alexi (Martin, 1984) was long lumped with specimen YPM 1478, described initially as Hesperornis gracilis and later moved to the monotypic genus Hargeria (Lucas, 1903).

facts.statement: The original description of the genus Hargeria was based exclusively on the specimen YPM 1478, which was the holotype of Hesperornis gracilis.
facts.quote: Nonetheless, the taxon description of Hargeria was about "Hesperornis" gracilis exclusively, and thus despite the misidentification it applies to YPM 1478, the holotype of "H." gracilis.

facts.statement: Later authors corrected the taxonomic confusion by synonymizing the genus Hargeria back into Hesperornis.
facts.quote: Esta equivocación fue rectificada por autores posteriores, quienes sinonimizaron nuevamente Hargeria con Hesperornis.

facts.statement: Fossils of Parahesperornis are found only in the upper Niobrara Chalk of Kansas, dating to the Coniacian-Santonian boundary between 85 and 82 million years ago.
facts.quote: Found only in the upper Niobrara Chalk, these are from around the Coniacian-Santonian boundary, 85–82 million years ago (mya).

facts.statement: Fossils of Parahesperornis are found only in the upper Niobrara Chalk, dating to the boundary between the Coniacian and Santonian stages, approximately 85 to 82 million years ago.
facts.quote: Hallado sólo en la parte superior de la caliza de Niobrara, sus fósiles están en torno al límite entre el Coniaciense al Santoniense, hace 85-82 millones de años.

facts.statement: The time range for Parahesperornis is estimated to be from the Coniacian to the Santonian, between 89.8 and 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Coniacian to Santonian (89.8 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Parahesperornis was a flightless, toothed seabird belonging to the Hesperornithes and is closely related to the genus Hesperornis.
facts.quote: Parahesperornis was a member of the Hesperornithes, flightless toothed seabirds of the Cretaceous and more specifically in the main lineage, close to Hesperornis.

facts.statement: Parahesperornis was a member of the Hesperornithes and was very closely related to Hesperornis.
facts.quote: Parahesperornis era miembro un miembro de Hesperornithes, muy cercano a Hesperornis.

facts.statement: In 2017, researchers considered the genus Asiahesperornis as a possible synonym of Parahesperornis.
facts.quote: In 2017, Asiahesperornis was considered as a possible synonym of Parahesperornis.

facts.statement: The diversity of Parahesperornis remains enigmatic because similar fossils found in Mongolia lack sufficient diagnostic features to confirm their classification.
facts.quote: However, they are not very diagnostic regardless, and the diversity of Parahesperornis remains enigmatic.

facts.statement: Remains of Parahesperornis are known from central North America, specifically from the former shallows of the Western Interior Seaway in Kansas.
facts.quote: Remains are known from central North America, namely the former shallows of the Western Interior Seaway in Kansas.

facts.statement: Parahesperornis originated in central North America and inhabited the ancient shallow waters of the Western Interior Seaway in Kansas.
facts.quote: Procedente de la zona central de Norteamérica, habitó en el antiguo mar poco profundo de la Vía Marítima Occidental en Kansas.

facts.statement: The temporal and geographic range of Parahesperornis appears to have been very extensive, but its evidence is very fragmentary and scarce compared to that of contemporary relatives like Hesperornis.
facts.quote: Su rango tanto temporal como geográfico parece haber sido muy extenso, pero su evidencia es muy fragmentaria y escasa, comparada con la de otros parientes suyos contemporáneos como Hesperornis.

facts.statement: It is possible that the genus Parahesperornis extended into the Campanian stage, to less than 80 million years ago.
facts.quote: Possibly the genus extended into the Campanian, to less than 80 mya.

facts.statement: It is possible that the genus extended until the Campanian epoch, less than 80 million years ago.
facts.quote: Posiblemente el género se extendiera hasta la época del Campaniense, hace menos de 80 millones de años.

facts.statement: Two similar fossils found in Mongolia are distal ends of tibiotarsi that resemble Hesperornithiformes bones and are specifically similar to Parahesperornis due to their small size.
facts.quote: Both are distal ends of tibiotarsi, and they seem certainly more similar to the bones of Hesperornithiformes and (due to the smallish size) to Parahesperornis specifically.

facts.statement: Both fossils are distal ends of tibiotarsi and appear very similar to Hesperornithiformes bones, and more specifically to Parahesperornis due to their small size.
facts.quote: Ambos son extremos distales de tibiotarsos, y parecen ser muy similares a los huesos de las aves Hesperornithiformes y más específicamente (debido a su pequeño tamaño) muy parecidos a Parahesperornis.
